evidence.ref: .warp/frontier.py computes the global claimable frontier: claimable(worker_caps, scope, repo_root, claims_root) returns the units a worker may claim across the whole repo - BUILD work (a ready spec whose plan deps are all shipped, across every ACTIVE plan (status ready or in_progress; draft plans yield nothing, released/closed have no frontier), reusing plan.py item_state/_shipped_set/_decision_blocks) plus standalone/bug ready specs, plus REVIEW work (a spec in status review awaiting its verdict, kind review). It excludes already-claimed units (claim.claimed_units), work whose requires are not a subset of worker_caps (claim.capability_ok), and out-of-scope work (a plan id or a label). Read-only. Repo reading is parametrized by repo_root and spec front matter is parsed with parse_yamlish so requires/labels are real lists. A warp frontier CLI lists it.

a selftest block drives claimable() over a temporary repo tree and a temporary claims root: a ready build with deps met, a standalone ready spec, and a pending review are claimable; a dependency-blocked build, a ready spec under a DRAFT plan, capability-gated work without the cap, an already-claimed unit, and out-of-scope work are excluded; non-tautological - with the capability the gated work appears and after a claim the unit drops out; reviewer independently reproduced all 5 ACs and confirmed the capability and claimed mutations each turn it red; part of selftest 1001 passed, 0 failed

It reuses the pure plan logic (item_state, shipped set, decision blocks) and the claim ledger (capability_ok, claimed_units), reimplementing neither. This is the read side; claiming a unit is WARP-0701 and driving it is WARP-0703. A REVIEW unit's claim keys on the spec id (integration with the worker loop, Y3).
